Package hadur2.core.model

Class RobotStateLog

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.model.RobotStateLog
All Implemented Interfaces:
Cloneable
public class RobotStateLog extends Object implements Cloneable
A robot's RobotStates keyed by tick, with linear interpolation across the ticks that were not observed.

Several parts of the core keep one. HadurCore logs our state and the duel enemy's at every scan and asks how far each robot has moved over the last 8, 20 and 40 ticks, which become wave attributes for the KNN views. Each active Wave in a WaveManager has a log of its target's states, from which the ticks the wave was crossing the target are recovered when it breaks. The surf fills logs with predicted states and clones them to branch on each option, and the melee brain keeps our own path.

Interpolation exists because states do not arrive every tick: the radar can miss a tick, and a skipped turn loses one, yet a wave's break is checked tick by tick. An interpolated state is marked RobotState.interpolated, is never used as an end point for another interpolation, and is stored so the next request for that tick is a lookup.

The log is bounded (RES-2): past MAX_STATES it drops the oldest tick. Its owners clear it or drop it at the start of each round, since ticks restart at 0.

    • getState

      public RobotState getState(long time, boolean interpolate)
      The state at time.

      A state held for that tick is returned as it is, unless it was interpolated and interpolate is false. Otherwise, with interpolate, the nearest observed states before and after it are blended linearly: location and velocity directly, and heading along the shorter way round. The result is stored in the log.

      Parameters:
      time - the tick wanted
      interpolate - whether a state may be made up from its neighbours
      Returns:
      the state, or null when there is none for that tick and it cannot be interpolated (no observed state on one side of it: the log never extrapolates)

    • getDisplacementDistance

      public double getDisplacementDistance(Point2D.Double location, long currentTime, long ticksAgo)
      Pixels between location and where the robot was ticksAgo ticks before currentTime (interpolated if need be). Early in a round, when the log does not reach that far back, the oldest state stands in, so the result is the distance moved so far. The log must hold at least one state.
      Parameters:
      location - the robot's location now, pixels
      currentTime - the current tick
      ticksAgo - how far back to look, ticks
      Returns:
      the straight-line distance, pixels
